items.title: E309's residue: a spaced generic METHOD call — `h.make <str>("a")` over `fun make<U>(self, u: U): U` — still gets the comparison's cascade ("struct 'Holder' has no field 'make'", "`bool` has no ordering", "`str` is a type, not a value"), none naming the spacing
items.body: E309 steers the spaced call when its name is a generic FUNCTION or a generic TYPE (a name or path resolved at the accessor); the member form reads `h.make` as a field access, which fails before anything knows `make` is a generic method of `Holder`. The same seam fits: `note_spaced_generic_call` admitting a `MemberAccessor(_, Accessor)` left side, the field refusal held like the type-in-value-position one, and the decision asking whether the receiver's type has a generic method of that name. Sizing XS-S; the analyzer.

items.title: A METHOD named without its call parentheses is refused as a missing FIELD — `p.norm` over `impl Point { fun norm(self): i32 }` says "struct 'Point' has no field 'norm'", and `<input .autofocus />` (an element head's bare link) says "struct 'View' has no field 'autofocus'" with E119's twin note claiming the browser twin declares it (both twins declare the METHOD); neither says `.norm()` / `.autofocus()`
items.body: The field refusal does not ask whether a method of that name exists. A steer — "`norm` is a method of `Point`: call it, `p.norm()`" — and E119's twin note asked about FIELDS only when the miss is a field the other twin has (it fires today because the browser twin's `autofocus` member is found by name, whatever kind it is). In an element head the bare form is likely the commonest way to meet it (`<input .autofocus />` beside `<input autofocus />`). Sizing S; the analyzer's field-accessor refusal.
